question: If the marked price of a calculator is ₹600 and ₹50 discount is offered on the calculator, then find the discount percentage (correct to two decimal places).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount % = (Discount ÷ Marked Price) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (50 ÷ 600) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 100 ÷ 12 = 8.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 8.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹600

Discount = ₹50

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

 
 
 
• 
 Selling Price = ₹550
 Disc = ₹50
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Marked Price = ₹600
 Discount % = (50 ÷ 600) × 100 = 8.33%

**Calculation:**

⇒ Discount % = (50 ÷ 600) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 12) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 100 ÷ 12

⇒ Discount % = 25 ÷ 3

⇒ Discount % ≈ 8.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 8.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price printed on the label of an article. Any discount offered to the customer is always calculated on this price.

Selling Price (SP)

The actual price paid by the buyer after the deduction of the discount. Rule: SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are provided, the effective net discount is equivalent to (a + b − a × b ÷ 100)%.
